result:
I could not derive the constant, and I could not recall the published result, so I cannot confirm that $\sqrt{2}$ is correct.

The proposed solution gives no real derivation. It describes a trace-method argument in general terms, then asserts that "the optimization of the moments and the application of Cauchy-Schwarz" gives exactly $\sqrt{2}$. No computation supports this value, and the solution presents no matching extremal construction showing it is sharp.

My own attempts did not settle the value either. A heuristic using only the edge-count constraint on initial segments of the Perron vector gave a bound of the wrong order. That means the constraint over all subsets matters, and the constant depends on how it is used. A random-graph check also gave no matching construction.

Because the justification is unsupported and the constant is unverified, I do not accept the answer.

VERDICT: REJECT
